analysis.title: Duttenhoefer's Daily 08.10.2026
key_insights: S&P 500 closed -22bps at 7802 (+14% YTD) in another quiet session. US 10yr unchanged at 5.31%, French 10yr higher at 4.86%.
$39bn US 10yr auction was decent, with a 2.77x bid-to-cover. Brent at $102 with no news, Gold at $4134, Bitcoin at $82.5k after big liquidations.
Yesterday's FOMC minutes had no major surprises. Earnings season starts next week, with JPM reporting on 13 Oct.

IMF article: global public debt is near its highest level since after WW2 and is on track to soon exceed 100% of GDP. Policymakers had an easy 17 years because interest rates stayed below GDP growth rates.
Texas grid operator's queue of large new customers grew from 63 GW in 2024 to 474 GW by June 2026, more than five times record peak demand. About 90% of it is data centers.

Google announced 'Playground', a browser-based platform for making custom games from AI prompts with no coding required. The author sees it as another feature that takes user time from incumbent platforms.

Tech positioning: overall market net positioning is low, but net exposure on GS prime book to Mag7 as % of total US exposure is near 22%, the highest on record. Semis are ~12% of total US exposure (vs 14% in June and 6% in Jan). US Tech had its largest % buying in a month since Feb 2025 in Sep and was the only sector net bought.

GS likes buying the Power Up America basket (GSENEPOW). It has underperformed other AI themes and the S&P 500 YTD. GS calls it the most underappreciated AI bottleneck, with low positioning, normalized valuation and intact fundamentals.

GS recommends buying the Consumer Experiences basket. Spending growth on experiences accelerated from 1% in Q1 2025 to 6% in Q1 2026. Valuations are attractive, revisions are close to inflecting and positioning is not crowded. Higher-income exposure has insulated the basket from higher fuel costs. Composition: 40% live entertainment, 20% leisure, 20% hotels, 20% cruises.

US semis preview: GS sees upside to estimates across most sub-sectors. After a pullback over the past 2 months (SOX -11% vs SPX +4%), the setup into earnings is more constructive, in contrast to the cautious tactical stance before Q2 results.

On US inflation, roughly 75% of the surprise came from mismeasurement or one-time factors expected to fade. GS sees no strong evidence of an acceleration in the underlying trend and forecasts core PCE falling to 2.2% by Dec 2027. The author asks whether this means Fed cuts in 2027.

Q3 earnings preview: consensus expects S&P 500 y/y EPS growth of 27%. AI infrastructure spending accounts for over 50% of S&P 500 EPS growth, alongside hyperscaler capex growth of 116%. Median S&P stock EPS growth is about 9% in Q3 vs 14% in Q2.
GS economists estimate higher rates will subtract only about 0.2% from GDP growth in 2027, based on housing, consumption and capex.

Mega-cap tech generated roughly $150bn of accounting profit last quarter from appreciating equity investment stakes, equal to 12% of S&P 500 EPS. GS does not expect a meaningful impact from similar other income this quarter.
